events.title: Node.js 4.0 released
events.summary: Node.js 4.0.0 shipped on September 8, 2015 — merging the io.js fork back into Node with V8 4.5, native ES6 support, and an LTS schedule.
events.about: Node 4 ended the io.js schism and established even-numbered LTS releases. Arrow functions, classes, and template literals worked natively; npm 2 shipped bundled. It became the baseline for Express, Koa, and the MEAN/MERN stacks of the mid-2010s.

narrative.whyChosen: Node 4 reunited the community after the io.js fork and defined modern Node LTS.
narrative.whyImportant: The LTS policy gave enterprises a stable line while odd versions experimented.
narrative.problemSolved: The io.js fork split contributors and left production teams unsure which runtime to ship.

events.title: Safari 9 released
events.summary: Apple released Safari 9 on September 30, 2015 with OS X El Capitan — adding pinned tabs, AirPlay support, and improved JavaScript performance.
events.about: Safari 9 refined the El Capitan experience with muteable tabs, content blocking extensions, and CSS scroll snapping. It kept WebKit competitive as mobile browsing overtook desktop for many sites.

narrative.whyChosen: Safari 9 added content blockers and pinned tabs that shaped desktop browsing habits.
narrative.whyImportant: Content blocking extensions changed the ad and privacy landscape on Mac.
narrative.problemSolved: Users wanted Safari-native ad blocking without third-party plugins like Flash.
